recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future SupplyRequest.deliverFor changes should be handled in HL7/oo-incubator after a final work-group decision, especially if FHIR-52991 progresses; do not edit inactive core SupplyRequest files for FHIR-39511.
issue_request: FHIR-39511 was a Published/Persuasive R5 Orders and Observations change request to add SupplyRequest subject/deliverFor, 0..1 Reference(Patient), with the requested patient-focused short and long definitions.
initial_application: Core history shows the issue was applied: fa4707d5a7 added the Patient reference as SupplyRequest.subject, and 2e15fce0f1 renamed the element and patient search parameter expression to SupplyRequest.deliverFor with subject as the alias. The legacy core SupplyRequest source still contains SupplyRequest.deliverFor 0..1 Reference(Patient) and SupplyRequest-patient points to SupplyRequest.deliverFor.
additional_context: The current core build no longer includes SupplyRequest in source/fhir.ini's active [resources] list. Commit 3b38b80cf2 removed SupplyRequest, SupplyDelivery, and related OO resources from core and redirected current narrative links to the OO Incubator IG. The OO Incubator continuous-build package contains SupplyRequest.deliverFor 0..1 Reference(Patient) and the patient search parameter expression SupplyRequest.deliverFor. FHIR-52991 is a later Triaged/unresolved OO Incubator issue about widening or renaming SupplyRequest/SupplyDelivery subject and destination actors, so it does not supersede FHIR-39511.
reconciliation: No core source files were changed. The current FHIR core checkout no longer owns active SupplyRequest definitions, and editing the inactive legacy source would not affect the current core build. The external current owner already carries the requested element.

related_jiras.note: Triaged/unresolved OO Incubator issue proposing broader SupplyRequest/SupplyDelivery subject and destination changes; not a final reversal and outside core.
Later Applied workflow-alignment issue mapped SupplyRequest.deliverFor to Request.subject, confirming the deliverFor/subject interpretation before the resource moved out of active core.
